name: Guni
overview: Guni was a male member of the tribe of Gad in ancient Israel. He is specifically noted as the father of Abdiel, marking his place in the genealogical records of the Gadites. Beyond this paternal link, Scripture provides no further details about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Guni means "spotted sand grouse," a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:15. This name does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a common Hebrew personal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Guni is identified as the father of Abdiel, establishing a direct familial line within the tribe of Gad. Additionally, he is noted as a descendant of Gad, underscoring his tribal affiliation. No other family relationships are recorded in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Guni's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role within the tribe of Gad. By being the father of Abdiel, he contributes to the preservation of the tribal lineage important for understanding Israel's tribal structure. His mention in 1 Chronicles 5:15 situates him within the broader biblical narrative of Israel's genealogy, emphasizing the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations.
